data.name: labs.automationextensions.recordresult.explanation
data.value: Saves whether this step succeeded, so a later "Previous step succeeded" condition can branch on it.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.resultsource.explanation
data.value: Type of the earlier step whose result is checked. The step must have "Record result for later steps" turned on.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.resultnumber.write.explanation
data.value: Select the same step and number in the "Previous step succeeded" condition. When a process has several steps of this type, give each one a different number.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.resultnumber.read.explanation
data.value: Number selected on the earlier step. If no earlier step saved this result, contacts follow the No branch.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.skipstep.action.explanation
data.value:
Contacts move on without this step running.
Use when you can't delete the step because the process already has contact history.
Tip: start the step name with "[Skipped]" (or ⏭️) so it's visible in the builder.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.skipstep.condition.explanation
data.value:
The condition isn't checked and all contacts follow the branch selected below.
This applies only when the component is enabled by your administrator.
If disabled by application configuration, all library conditions follow No, regardless of this setting.
Use when you can't delete the step because the process already has contact history.
Tip: start the step name with "[Skipped → Yes]" or "[Skipped → No]" so it's visible in the builder.
If you turn skipping off later, make sure both branches lead to further steps.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.skippedbranch.explanation
data.value: Branch all contacts follow while the step is skipped.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.description
data.value: Sends the contact to an external system (CRM, CDP, Zapier, Power Automate). Endpoints are set up by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.endpoint.explanation
data.value:
System that receives the contact.
Missing a destination?
Ask your developers to add it to the application configuration.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.eventname.explanation
data.value: Tells the receiving system what happened, for example "lead-qualified" or "webinar-registered".

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.includecontactdetails.explanation
data.value:
Adds email, first name, last name, and company name.
Leave off to send only an anonymous contact ID.
Only enable when the destination is allowed to receive personal data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.description
data.value: Posts a message about the contact to a Microsoft Teams or Slack channel configured by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.channel.explanation
data.value:
Teams or Slack channel that receives the message.
Channels are configured by your developers.
Missing a channel? Ask them to add it to the application configuration.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.title.explanation
data.value: Optional heading, for example Hot lead: {contact.ContactFirstName} {contact.ContactLastName}. Placeholders as in the message.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.message.explanation
data.value:
Plain text, line breaks are kept. Placeholders:
{now} – current date and time, {today} – current date.
{processName}, {triggerIdentifier}, {contactId}, {contactGuid}.
{contact.FieldName} – value of a contact field, for example {contact.ContactEmail}.
{triggerData.PropertyName} – data of the trigger that started the process.
Unknown placeholders become empty and a warning is logged.
Contact fields in placeholders leave Xperience like contact details do.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.includecontactdetails.explanation
data.value:
Adds email, name, and company name.
Personal data leaves Xperience and is visible to everyone in the channel.
Only enable when the channel is allowed to receive personal data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.includeadminlink.explanation
data.value: Adds a link that opens the contact in the Xperience administration. Only works when your developers configured the administration URL.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.includeformsubmissionlink.label
data.value: Include link to the form submission

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.includeformsubmissionlink.explanation
data.value: Only for processes started by a form submission. Adds a link that opens the submitted form data in the Xperience administration. Only works when your developers configured the administration URL.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.postchatmessage.includeprocesslink.explanation
data.value: Adds a link that opens the Contacts tab of this automation process. The process is found by its name: no link is added when several processes share the name. Only works when your developers configured the administration URL.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.description
data.value: Writes a message to the Event log for every contact reaching this step. Use to check which path contacts take. Usually enabled only during testing.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.message.explanation
data.value:
Text written to the log.
You can use {processName}, {contactId}, {contactGuid}, and {triggerIdentifier}.
Don't include personal data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.level.explanation
data.value: Use Warning or Error for paths that need attention, for example when a webhook failed.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.includestepresults.explanation
data.value: Adds results saved by earlier steps, for example whether "Send webhook" succeeded. Helps explain why a "Previous step succeeded" condition took a branch.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.includetriggerdetails.explanation
data.value: Adds what started the process, for example the submitted form or the contact date.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.previousstepsucceeded.description
data.value: Checks whether an earlier step (for example "Send webhook") succeeded. Use after a step with "Record result for later steps" turned on.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.description
data.value: Assigns each contact to a stable Yes (A) or No (B) branch. Requires administrator enablement; when disabled by application configuration, all contacts follow No (B), regardless of skip settings.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.percentage.explanation
data.value:
When enabled by your administrator, this percentage (0–100) of contacts follows Yes (A); the rest follow No (B).
Allocation is approximate, not an exact count.
When disabled by application configuration, all contacts follow No (B), regardless of this percentage or skip settings.
Ask your administrator to confirm whether this component is enabled.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.splitkey.explanation
data.value:
Stable name for this split, default "default".
Same contact and key always get the same bucket, even after a process is renamed.
Keys are case-sensitive; spaces matter.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.splitkey.required
data.value: Enter a split key containing at least one non-space character.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactdateanniversary.description
data.value: Starts once a year on (or before) a contact date, such as a birthday. Runs daily – requires a scheduled task set up by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactdateanniversary.datefield.explanation
data.value:
Only the month and day are used, so the process starts every year.
Missing a field?
Ask your developers to add it to the application configuration.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactdateanniversary.daysbefore.explanation
data.value: Start on the date or a number of days before it. Set the process recurrence to "If not already running" ("Only once" would start it only in the first year).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactinactive.description
data.value: Starts when a contact's last activity was exactly the selected number of days ago – requires a scheduled task set up by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactinactive.inactivedays.explanation
data.value:
Starts once on the day the contact's last activity (of any type) reaches this number of days.
Missing a value?
Ask your developers to add it to the application configuration.
Contacts without any activity never start the process.
If the scheduled task doesn't run on a day, contacts reaching the value that day aren't started later.
If the task runs more than once a day, set the process recurrence to "If not already running" and keep contacts in the process for at least one day (e.g. with a Wait step).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactgroupmember.description
data.value: Starts for contacts in the selected contact group, checked once per day – requires a scheduled task set up by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactgroupmember.contactgroup.explanation
data.value:
Only contact groups listed in the application configuration can be selected.
Missing a group?
Ask your developers to add it to the application configuration. Recipient lists aren't supported.
Fires every day for every contact in the group, not only for new members. Set the process recurrence to "If not already running" or "Only once" – "Always" restarts the process for every member every day.
Group membership is updated by Xperience's contact group recalculation and can lag behind.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactgroupmember.contactgroup.format
data.comment: {0} = contact group display name, {1} = contact group code name

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.description
data.value: Checks if the current time (when this condition runs) falls within a configured time window. This is NOT a Wait step – time is evaluated immediately.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.starttime.explanation
data.value: Window opens at this time, inclusive (e.g., 2:00 PM / 14:00 is included). For overnight windows (e.g., 10:00 PM–2:00 AM / 22:00–02:00), the selected weekday refers to the day the window starts.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.endtime.explanation
data.value: Window closes at this time, exclusive (e.g., 4:00 PM / 16:00 is not included). Can be earlier than start time for overnight windows (e.g., 10:00 PM–2:00 AM / 22:00–02:00).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.timezone.explanation
data.value:
The host's local time zone.
UTC is the default.
The time zone ID is saved and must exist on any deployment host.
Zones not available on deployment hosts cause an error – contact your administrator.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.startdate.explanation
data.value: Limits the time window to dates on or after this date, inclusive. Leave blank for no limit.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.enddate.explanation
data.value:
Limits the time window to dates on or before this date, inclusive.
Leave blank for no limit.
Must be on or after the start date.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.stepregistry.scope.content
data.value:
This tab lists the registered trigger, action, and condition definitions for the whole application, not just this process. It does not inspect which steps this process uses.

Status shows the effective state of library components; the default is disabled unless application configuration enables them.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.stepregistry.disabled.content
data.value:
When a library condition is disabled, all contacts follow the "No" path without evaluating the condition. Administrator disablement overrides marketer skip settings.
Disabled library actions do nothing (contacts continue); disabled library triggers cannot start processes. All disabled steps log warnings in the Event Log when run.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.adjustcontactscore.description
data.value: Changes a number field of the contact (add, subtract, or set), with an optional minimum and maximum. Requires an integer custom contact field.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.adjustcontactscore.field.explanation
data.value:
Contact field that stores the score.
Lists custom contact fields of the integer type; ask your developer to add one if the list is empty.
Empty values count as 0.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.adjustcontactscore.operation.explanation
data.value:
Add: increases the current score by the amount.
Subtract: decreases the current score by the amount.
Set: replaces the current score with the amount.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.adjustcontactscore.amount.explanation
data.value: Points to add or subtract, or the new score for Set. Use 0 or more; the operation sets the direction.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.adjustcontactscore.limitrange.explanation
data.value: Keeps the new score between the minimum and maximum (both included). Applies to all operations.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.adjustcontactscore.minimum.explanation
data.value: Lowest allowed score. Must not be greater than the maximum, otherwise the step does nothing.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.description
data.value: Sets a contact field to a value built from placeholders (date, process, trigger data, other fields) or calculates a number from the current value.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.field.explanation
data.value:
Contact field to change. Custom fields are listed first, built-in fields are marked as system fields.
Built-in fields drive Xperience features (for example, the email address is used for recipient lists and contact matching), so prefer custom fields.
Fields maintained by Xperience (IDs, created and modified dates, bounces) aren't listed.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.mode.explanation
data.value:
Set to value: replaces the field value with the value below (placeholders allowed).
Calculate: combines the current number with an operand, for example + 1. Only for number fields.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.valuetemplate.explanation
data.value:
Text and placeholders, for example Spring sale or {processName}.
{now} – current date and time, {today} – current date.
{processName}, {triggerIdentifier}, {contactId}, {contactGuid}.
{contact.FieldName} – value of another contact field.
{triggerData.PropertyName} – data of the trigger that started the process, for example {triggerData.InactiveDays}.
Unknown placeholders become empty and a warning is logged.
Numbers use a dot as decimal separator, dates yyyy-MM-dd, yes/no fields true or false.
An empty value clears the field.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.onlyifempty.label
data.value: Only if the field is empty

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.onlyifempty.explanation
data.value: Leaves fields that already have a value unchanged. The step still counts as succeeded.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.operator.explanation
data.value:
Calculates: current value, operator, operand. An empty field counts as 0.
Whole-number fields divide without decimals (7 ÷ 2 = 3).
Division by zero or a result outside the field's range fails the step without changing the field.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.operand.explanation
data.value:
Number combined with the current value, for example 1 or 2.5 (dot as decimal separator).
Placeholders are allowed, for example {triggerData.Years}.
Whole-number fields accept whole numbers only.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.setcontactfield.resultnumber.explanation
data.value: The step always saves whether it succeeded. Select the same step and number in the "Previous step succeeded" condition. When a process has several steps of this type, give each one a different number.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactnumberfieldcompare.description
data.value: Checks whether an integer custom contact field (for example a score set by "Adjust contact score") is equal to, greater than, or less than a value; empty fields count as 0.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactnumberfieldcompare.field.explanation
data.value:
Contact field to compare, for example the score field of "Adjust contact score".
Lists custom contact fields of the integer type; ask your developer to add one if the list is empty.
Empty values count as 0.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactnumberfieldcompare.operator.explanation
data.value: Contacts whose field value matches follow Yes; all others follow No.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactnumberfieldcompare.operator.greaterthanorequal
data.value: is greater than or equal to

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactnumberfieldcompare.operator.lessthanorequal
data.value: is less than or equal to

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactnumberfieldcompare.value.explanation
data.value: Whole number the field value is compared with. Negative numbers are allowed.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.description
data.value: Checks which trigger started the process and, optionally, a value of its trigger data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.trigger.explanation
data.value: Built-in triggers and all triggers registered in the application. Contacts whose process was started by this trigger follow Yes; all others follow No.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.checktriggerdata.explanation
data.value: Follow Yes only when a value of the trigger data also matches. Shown only for triggers that provide data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.field.explanation
data.value:
Data field of the selected trigger.
Changing the trigger clears the field.
If the trigger no longer has the field, all contacts follow No.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.operator.explanation
data.value:
Is equal to, is not equal to: any field (numbers and dates by value).
Contains, does not contain, starts with, ends with: the field value as text.
Greater than, less than: number and date fields only.
Is empty, is not empty: any field, no value needed.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.operator.greaterthanorequal
data.value: is greater than or equal to

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.operator.lessthanorequal
data.value: is less than or equal to

data.name: labs.automationextensions.startedbytrigger.value.explanation
data.value:
Numbers with a dot as decimal separator, for example 12.5.
Dates as yyyy-MM-dd, for example 2026-10-11 (time is ignored).
Text ignores upper and lower case; yes/no values are true or false.
Don't enter personal data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.description
data.value: Checks how many times the contact performed an activity type in the last N days (for example 3 or more page visits in 7 days); to check whether a contact performed an activity at all, use the built-in Rule-based condition.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.activitytype.explanation
data.value: Type of activity to count. Lists enabled activity types.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.operator.explanation
data.value: Contacts whose number of activities matches follow Yes; all others follow No.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.count.explanation
data.value: Whole number the activity count is compared with, for example 3.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.days.explanation
data.value: Counts activities logged in the last N × 24 hours up to now (server time). Enter 1–365.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.textoperator.explanation
data.value: How the text below is matched (not case-sensitive with the default database collation).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.urlrules.explanation
data.value:
Optional; counts only activities whose URL matches all rules. No rules = all URLs.
Page visit, landing page, form submission: the page URL. Email link click: the clicked link.
Not case-sensitive; fragments (#…), default ports, and trailing slashes are ignored, and the path never includes the query string.
Use Test a URL to see the compared parts. The referrer URL isn't searched.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.title.explanation
data.value:
Optional; leave empty to count all activities of the type.
Compares only the name in quotes of the stored title, for example Home in Page visit 'Home' – is equal to Home doesn't match Home page.
Page visit, landing page: page name.
Form submission: form name.
Member registration: member name or email.
Email link click: email name.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.value.explanation
data.value:
Optional; leave empty to count all activities of the type.
Compares the value logged with the activity (custom and other activity types).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.pages.explanation
data.value:
Optional; counts only activities on the selected pages (any of them). Leave empty to count all pages.
Works only for pages from the content tree tracked by Xperience – matched by page, so URL changes, query strings, and fragments don't matter.
For other URLs use URL rules.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.activityfrequency.language.explanation
data.value: Optional; counts only activities on this language version of the pages. Any counts all languages.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.value.pattern
data.value: Use * for any characters, for example /blog/*

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.test.match
data.value: Matches all rules – the activity counts.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.test.nomatch
data.value: Doesn't match – the activity doesn't count.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.test.unrecognized
data.value: Not a recognized URL – it matches only "is not equal to", "does not contain", and "is not present" rules.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.test.timedout
data.value: A pattern took too long to compare and counts as not matching. Simplify the pattern.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.test.failed
data.value: The URL couldn't be tested. Try again.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.error.invalidjson
data.value: The saved URL rules can't be read. Remove the rules and add them again.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.error.unsupportedversion
data.value: The saved URL rules have an unsupported format. Remove the rules and add them again.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.error.operatornotallowed
data.value: The operator isn't available for this URL part.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.urlmatch.error.parametertoolong
data.value: Enter a parameter name of at most {2} characters.
